summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Zurich (1835–1838, Habilitation ~1840–1841) under Hirzel, von Orelli, and Sauppe. He held posts at Zurich (1841–1889), Kantonsschule Rämibühl (~1841–1889), and Höhere Töchterschule Zürich (~1876–1894).

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (~1865–1870) studying under Hermann Brockhaus. He subsequently served as a teacher of classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD ~1875–1879), and Leipzig (Habilitation ~1883–1886), as well as under Jäschke, Feer, Gabelentz, and Max Müller. He held a Habilitation post at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Roth, Goldschmidt, Scherer, Windisch, and Weber. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald (1881), Heidelberg, and Columbia University, and was a Prussian Academy member (1902).

Heinrich von Stietencron worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Munich (1957–1965), SOAS, and Heidelberg (Habilitation ~1965–1972). He served as an assistant at Heidelberg (1965) and held a chair at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.

Heinz Bechert was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, Mainz (doctorate ~1956), and under Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Saarland University (~1957–1964), Mainz (1964–1965), and the Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Mode was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, under Malalasekera and Fischer, and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at Basel. From 1948 to 1978, he served as professor of Oriental archaeology at Halle-Wittenberg.

Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University (PhD under Paul B. Watt) before taking up a post at the University of Hawaiʻi in ~1993.

Helen Hardacre works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Vanderbilt, Chicago (PhD under Kitagawa and Smith), and under Hitoshi Miyake, she held appointments at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith University (1990–1992), and Harvard University beginning in 1992.

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and has served as Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum since ~1993.
Helena Blankleder is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984 and held an academic post at Rice University starting around ~1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1960–1967). She served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a scholar of linguistics who held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1935–1941) and the University of Cologne (~1941–1970).

Hellmut Wilhelm was a sinologist who studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin (doctorate ~1928–1932 under Otto Franke). He held posts at Frankfurt, Peking University (~1933–1948), and held the Chair of Sinology at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1945–1948) and under Paul Debes. He served as a Referent at the Forschungsstelle für Völkerrecht und Ausländisches Öffentliches Recht from ~1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Uppsala under Johansson and in 1905–1906 under Pischel and Geldner. He served as Dozent for Indology at Lund (1921) and professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Berlin, and Bonn (Promotion ~1964–1974), where he was taught by Frank-Richard Hamm. He held a post at the University of Bonn from ~1975 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Freiburg, Berlin (doctorate under Lüders), and Marburg, and held posts at the Prussian Academy, Ahnenerbe, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his Promotion (1989) and Habilitation (2002) at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and directed the IKGA (2007–2014).
